headline: Senate Impeachment Court Drops Fixed 16-Vote Threshold in Sara Duterte Trial
seoTitle: Senate Court Drops Fixed 16-Vote Threshold in Duterte Trial | FMB News
seoDescription: The Senate impeachment court ruled that the two-thirds conviction threshold in Vice President Sara Duterte’s trial will be calculated from senators legally and factually capable of participating when judgment is rendered.
deck: By a 13-1 vote, with six senator-judges not participating, the impeachment court overturned its earlier fixed 16-vote interpretation. The ruling does not itself establish a new fixed number: the denominator will depend on who is legally and factually capable of voting when judgment is rendered.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Senate, sitting as an impeachment court, overturned its earlier interpretation that 16 votes would always be required to convict Vice President Sara Duterte. The court voted 13-1 to adopt a formula based on senator-judges who remain legally and factually capable of participating when judgment is rendered; six senator-judges did not participate in the threshold vote.

The ruling means senators who are detained or suspended or otherwise legally restrained, sought by authorities with unknown whereabouts, physically or medically incapacitated, beyond the Senate’s coercive processes, or similarly situated may be excluded from the denominator if supported by competent and sufficient evidence.

sections.heading: What is confirmed
paragraphs: The Philippine News Agency reported the court’s completed ruling and vote. Reuters independently reported that the Senate impeachment court lowered the number of votes prosecutors may need to secure a conviction. Inquirer and GMA News independently covered the threshold proceedings.
The court also ruled that fractional two-thirds results must be rounded upward. For example, a 20-member denominator would require 14 votes, because 13 would be below two-thirds.

sections.heading: What is not yet decided
paragraphs: The September 23 ruling does not automatically set a single new numerical conviction threshold. The actual denominator must be determined from the senator-judges legally and factually capable of participating when the final judgment vote occurs.
The ruling is pro hac vice, meaning it governs this proceeding and is not a formal amendment of the Senate impeachment rules. Any future judicial challenge and its outcome remain unresolved.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The threshold dispute arose because several senator-judges have been unable to participate in the trial. Presiding officer Francis Escudero had ruled on July 6 that the Constitution’s requirement of two-thirds of all Senate members meant 16 votes in a 24-member chamber. Senator-Judge Erwin Tulfo challenged that interpretation on September 8.
This is a procedural continuation of FMB News’ ongoing coverage of Duterte’s impeachment trial. Earliest relevant FMB News report: /news/sara-duterte-impeachment-saln-day-25-september-15-2026.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: The ruling changes the mathematical framework that will govern any eventual verdict. Depending on how many senator-judges qualify to participate at judgment, prosecutors could need fewer than the previously fixed 16 votes, while the constitutional two-thirds requirement itself remains in force.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for the court’s eventual determination of which senator-judges belong in the voting denominator, any Supreme Court challenge, and the continuation of evidence and arguments on the articles of impeachment. The ruling is procedural and is not a finding that Duterte is guilty or not guilty of any impeachment charge.
